subject: Minimum first-token (TTFT) targets + streaming cadence (SSE vs WebSocket) — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Torres <maya@averysys.com>, ops@averysys.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Minimum first-token (TTFT) targets + streaming cadence (SSE vs WebSocket) — post-demo recap

Hi Maya / Avery ops team —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope the pilot: 

Key perf targets you called out during the call:
- First meaningful token (TTFT) target: <= 200 ms p50 for single-request prompts (interactive chat flows).
- Throughput baseline: 120 concurrent conversational users (50 active requests/sec average), with bursts to 300 concurrent.
- Streaming behavior: client wants incremental tokens flushed to the UI every ~60–120 ms during generation for a smooth typing experience.

Operational constraints we heard:
- Many end-users are on corporate networks with aggressive proxies; SSE is preferable for quick fallbacks but there are cases where WebSocket might be required.
- They will route traffic through a single egress IP for the pilot (important for sticky routing).

Proposed qualification plan (high level):
1) Quick probe run: we run a 1-hour TTFT probe against a representative prompt set at your pre-prod endpoint to measure p50/p90 TTFT, and chunk cadence. (We’ll provide ttft_probe_script.sh.)
2) Canary pilot: start with SSE streaming with 2s chunk-window (approx chunk every 80–120 ms depending on tokens/sec). If client-side proxies cause SSE failures, failover to WebSocket for affected segments.
3) Success criteria: p50 TTFT <= 200 ms; p95 TTFT <= 450 ms; chunk flush interval <= 200 ms for 95% of frames during steady-state.

Attachments: I’m attaching a simple perf matrix and the probe script we discussed. Also linking a short playbook for SSE vs WS fallbacks.

Next steps:
- Maya: confirm a 2-hour window next week for the probe (we recommend Tue/Wed morning PST).
- Karthik: we’ll need one engineer on the Avery side to pair during the probe to toggle client settings.
- Lauren: I’ll prep the pilot SOW and calendar invites once probe timing is confirmed.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: avery_perf_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), ttft_probe_script.sh (bash script), sse_vs_ws_playbook.pdf (doc)
From: Maya Torres <maya@averysys.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@averysys.com, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minimum first-token (TTFT) targets + streaming cadence (SSE vs WebSocket) — post-demo recap

Ben —

Thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our infra/ops side: 
- Our real-world p50 target is actually tighter for the main customer-facing chat: <= 150 ms if possible. The 200 ms you called out is acceptable as an initial threshold, but we’ll flag any p50 above 150 ms as a blocker for GA.
- For chunk cadence we mean the UI should receive small updates frequently (ideally 50–100 ms when generating up to ~15 tokens/sec). Anything over 200 ms feels noticeably choppy.
- Regarding proxies: our SRE team can open longer-lived SSE connections but some legacy clients will need WebSocket. We’ll need a simple fallback matrix we can give to our mobile/dev teams.

We can make an engineer available on Wed 14 Apr 2027 at 10:00 AM PST for the probe window.

Also, question on test data: can you run the probe with both the short-chat prompts and a worst-case long-prompt (18k tokens) to show degradation characteristics? We want to understand tail behavior.

Maya
Maya Torres
Director, Product Ops — Avery Systems

Subject: Re: Minimum first-token (TTFT) targets + streaming cadence (SSE vs WebSocket) — post-demo recap

Maya —

Great — Wed 14 Apr at 10:00 AM PST works for us. Quick answers inline: 
- We’ll aim the pilot to show p50 <= 150 ms for the short-chat set; the initial band we measure today will inform whether we need a different model/quant profile or routing tweak.
- We will run the probe with both prompt sets: short-chat (typical back-and-forth) and long-prompt (18k token) to capture the tail. Expect natural TTFT increase for long-context loads; we’ll capture p50/p90/p99.
- I’m attaching a short SSE vs WS fallback cheat-sheet (sse_vs_ws_playbook.pdf) for your mobile/dev teams; it lists header-level differences, keep-alive strategies, and typical proxy failure modes.

For the probe we plan to:
- Run 30-minute baseline at 1–2 QPS to validate single-request TTFT.
- Ramp to 50 QPS (simulating 120 concurrent users) for 20 minutes to validate throughput.
- Run a 10-minute burst test to 120 QPS to observe cold-cache TTFT and model fallback behavior.

Karthik — can you confirm the probe endpoint and whether we should enable prefix KV caching for the baseline run?

Ben

Attachments: sse_vs_ws_playbook.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Maya Torres <maya@averysys.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minimum first-token (TTFT) targets + streaming cadence (SSE vs WebSocket) — probe plan and config

Maya / Ben —

Thanks — quick technical checklist and a few asks before Wed’s probe: 

1) Endpoint & creds: Please provide the pre-prod endpoint and an API key for the probe. If you prefer, we can run from our end against your egress IP (you mentioned single-eip pilot).
2) Caching: For the short-chat probe we will enable prefix KV caching (safe for your prompts) — that will help bring p50 into the 100–150 ms band. For the long 18k token prompt we will run without prefix caching to show worst-case behavior.
3) Chunk cadence config: we’ll start with a server-side target of ~80 ms flush interval (configurable). Please let us know if your client needs smaller frames (we can reduce to ~50 ms but that increases CPU tokenization overhead).
4) Concurrency/threads: We need a test account that mimics 120 concurrent users; a single API key with header X-Test-Concurrency is fine.

Probe deliverables we’ll provide immediately after the run:
- p50/p90/p99 TTFT for both prompt sets
- Chunk flush interval distribution (histogram) and example SSE/WebSocket frames
- A short list of suggested runtime knob changes (model quant profile, batching window, KV cache) to reach p50 <= 150 ms where feasible

Operational note: if SSE connections are being dropped by intermediate proxies, we’ll instrument a fallback to WebSocket for those clients and report percentage of sessions impacted.

I’ll be on the call Wed 10:00 AM PST to pair with your engineer.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Minimum first-token (TTFT) targets + streaming cadence (SSE vs WebSocket) — confirmed probe & next steps

Maya / team —

Thanks for confirming the probe window yesterday. Quick status + next steps: 

1) Confirmed probe: Wed 14 Apr 2027, 10:00–12:00 PST — we ran the tests and I’m attaching the quick-pass results (summary below).

Summary highlights (short-chat prompts, default model w/ prefix caching enabled):
- p50 TTFT: 138 ms
- p90 TTFT: 310 ms
- p95 TTFT: 420 ms
- Chunk flush median: 85 ms; 95th percentile: 190 ms

Long-prompt (18k token, no prefix caching):
- p50 TTFT: 412 ms
- p90 TTFT: 980 ms
- p99 TTFT: 2.1 s

Key observations:
- We hit your p50 <= 150 ms goal for short-chat with prefix KV caching and current model/quant profile.
- Long-context workloads still show a significant TTFT tail; recommended mitigation is either truncated context before initial response, background KV warmup, or a lighter-weight short-context encoder for the initial token.
- SSE performed well during the baseline; ~0.8% of sessions experienced proxy-related SSE resets and we observed clean failover to WebSocket for those clients.

Action items / agreed next steps:
- Avery: confirm whether you want us to pursue a short-context encoder experiment (adds ~2–3 engineer-weeks) vs conservative mitigation (context trimming + cache priming).
- Redwood (Karthik): produce a short-run tech note with specific runtime knobs we recommend (batch window, target flush interval, model quant profile). Due: 2027-04-19.
- Ben / Lauren: draft pilot SOW for a 30-day pilot with SLAs tied to p50 TTFT and chunk cadence.

If this looks right I’ll push the summary deck and the raw CSVs to the Drive link I shared and spin up the SOW draft.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
